reason: Prepare the new membrane needed for cell growth and division.
expectation: Phospholipids and proteins will form new membrane material, though its exact form is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Copying DNA is also a goal, but I chose to prepare membrane first.

effect: The membrane supply is packaged in vesicles routed through the ER and Golgi, and can now enlarge the cell.
reaction: The delivery route makes the membrane-building step more concrete.
reason: Use the prepared membrane supply to advance the new growth goal.
expectation: The vesicles will deliver membrane to the cell surface, enlarging the cell.

alternatives.reason: DNA copying is also required, but I prefer to finish the membrane sequence first.

effect: The cell has grown by adding membrane, but its nuclear DNA still needs copying.
reaction: The fusion inset clearly connects vesicle delivery to growth.
reason: Copy the nuclear DNA so each eventual daughter can receive a complete genome.
expectation: The nucleotides will be used to copy the cell's nuclear DNA.

alternatives.reason: The spindle is also needed, but DNA must be copied for chromosome separation to be useful.

effect: The DNA is copied into joined sister copies, ready for spindle-mediated separation.
reaction: The old-and-new strand inset makes the copying mechanism clear.
reason: Build the spindle needed to separate the copied chromosomes; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: Proteins and duplicated centrosomes will form a chromosome-moving spindle.

effect: The spindle preview shows tubulin fibres assembling from two centrosomes after DNA copying; it is ready to be applied to the cell.
reaction: The timing caption clarifies that this is a preview rather than an already attached spindle.
reason: Use the spindle to separate the copied chromosomes; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: The spindle will separate sister copies and help form two daughter nuclei.

effect: The spindle separated the sister copies into two complete daughter nuclei, but the cytoplasm remains connected.
reaction: The time-strip makes the distinction between nuclear and cytoplasmic division clear.
reason: Use actin and myosin to divide the cytoplasm; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: Actin and myosin will constrict the furrow and separate the cell into two daughters.

effect: The cytoplasm has separated into two daughter stem cells, each with a complete genome; the chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The final picture usefully distinguishes self-renewal from later differentiation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using the spindle to form two nuclei was most worthwhile: the planned time-strip connects chromosome separation to complete genomes while showing that the cytoplasm is still joined.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the spindle was a necessary but relatively prescribed step: it was the only combination offered, and its assembly was presented as a preview rather than an interaction with chromosomes.

surprise.text: The membrane supply traveled through the ER and Golgi in vesicles before being added to the surface, giving cell growth a more concrete delivery route than I expected.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the spindle description introduces tubulin without explaining what it is beyond showing paired units forming fibres.

continue.text: I would continue: the separation of nuclear and cytoplasmic division and the prospect of cells taking different paths make the next constructions interesting.
